title: Go: Command Pattern
description: Implement the Command design pattern in Go to encapsulate requests as objects, supporting queuing, logging, and undo.

steps.title: Command interface and concrete commands
steps.description: Define a `Command` interface with `Execute() error`. Create concrete commands: `PrintCommand{Message string}` and `AddCommand{A, B int, Result *int}`. Implement Execute for both. Create and run them through an `Invoker`. Print results using `fmt.Printf("Executed: %s\n", description)`.
hints: Concrete commands hold all needed state
Invoker triggers Execute without knowing the details

verification.successMessage: Command interface and concrete commands work!

steps.title: Command queue and invoker
steps.description: Create a `CommandQueue` that maintains a slice of commands. Add `Enqueue(cmd Command)` and `ExecuteAll() error` methods that run each command sequentially. Queue 3 different commands and execute them all at once. Print the queue processing using `fmt.Printf("Queue[%d]: executing %T\n", pos, cmd)`.
hints: Queue stores commands for later execution
ExecuteAll iterates and runs each command
Commands can be reordered or scheduled

verification.failureMessage: Print each queued command with its position and type.

steps.title: Undo support
steps.description: Add an `Undo()` method to the Command interface. Implement undo for each command. Create a history stack in the invoker. After executing commands, undo the last one. Print undo operations using `fmt.Printf("Undo: %s\n", description)`.
hints: Each command must store reverse state for undo
Pop from stack and call Undo() in reverse order

verification.failureMessage: Print each undo operation with its description.

steps.title: Composite command (macro)
steps.description: Create a `MacroCommand` that holds a slice of commands and executes them in sequence. Implement `Execute()` and `Undo()` for it (undo executes child undos in reverse). Build a macro that performs a multi-step operation. Print macro execution using `fmt.Printf("Macro[%d steps]: %s\n", len(steps), name)`.
hints: Composite pattern: treat group as individual
Undo reverses children in opposite order

verification.failureMessage: Print the macro name and number of steps.
